## Objective
- Improve **Webweaver Wilds** with scarier, more visually distinct spiders, less repetitive overworld music, special battle music, more UI options, and controller support.

## Requirements
- Spiders should differ in shape and appearance, not just color, and look scarier.
- Battles should have special music; overworld music should be less repetitive.
- Add more UI options and controller support.

## Decisions
- Keep the existing self-contained canvas game and synthesized music; add species-specific silhouettes and markings, separate music patterns, and menu-based options.

## Work State
### Completed
- Added species-specific spider silhouettes, markings, legs, eyes, and fangs in `index.html`.
- Expanded the field menu with journal, supplies, party, and options pages; options include music, battle pace, high contrast, and controller status.
- Added separate synthesized overworld and battle music patterns with transitions on encounter and battle exit.
- Added Gamepad API polling and controls for confirm, cancel, menu, D-pad, and analog stick; connected polling to the render loop.
- Wired the header Options button to open the options page.
- JavaScript syntax check passed using `sed -n '/<script>/,/<\\/script>/p' index.html | sed '1d;$d' > /tmp/opencode/webweaver.js && node --check /tmp/opencode/webweaver.js`.

### Active
- Browser-test the updated menu, settings, gamepad support, spider appearances, and music transitions; fix any issues found.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Run the game in a browser and inspect runtime errors and visuals.
2. Test field-menu options, controller polling, and battle/overworld music transitions; correct any defects.

## Relevant Files
- `index.html`: Entire game implementation, including recent spider, menu, music, and controller changes.
- `capture.sh`: Existing browser screenshot capture entry point.
- `start.sh`: Existing preview server entry point.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted; project files are untracked in git.
- The previous checkpoint’s core game verification predates these recent modifications; the latest changes have only had a JavaScript syntax check.
